speaker: Doctor
text: Hello, I am Dr. Agent. You mentioned having a low-grade fever, an itchy rash, and joint pain after taking antibiotics; can you tell me which antibiotic you were prescribed and for what infection? Did your symptoms start before or after you finished the medication?

speaker: Patient
text: 8-year-old girl. The patient was brought to the emergency department because of a 2-day history of low-grade fever, itchy rash, and generalized joint pain. The rash initially started in the antecubital and popliteal fossae before spreading to the trunk and distal extremities. One week ago, she was diagnosed with acute sinusitis and started on amoxicillin. She has no history of adverse drug reactions, and her immunizations are up to date.

speaker: Doctor
text:
DIAGNOSIS READY: Amoxicillin-induced morbilliform drug eruption.

The clinical picture of a rash appearing one week after initiating amoxicillin, combined with fever and arthralgia, strongly supports this diagnosis. Given her age and symptom distribution, I would like to confirm the specific timing of symptom onset relative to the medication schedule. Could you clarify if the rash appeared while she was still taking the antibiotics or shortly after completing the course?

REQUEST TEST: Complete blood count (CBC) with differential.
REQUEST IMAGES: Full body skin examination photos.
